title: India Extends Contract Manufacturing Tax Breaks to 2041, Handing Apple a Major Expansion Win
excerpt: A proposed amendment would give foreign electronics firms a 15-year tax exemption on machinery and components supplied to Indian contract manufacturers, up from the five-year window set in February.
body:
• India has proposed extending tax exemptions for foreign companies supplying machinery to contract manufacturers from 2031 to March 2041 — a 15-year window.
  • The amendment is a direct win for Apple, which lobbied against Indian tax laws that could treat equipment ownership as a taxable “business connection.”
  • India now produces 26% of the world’s iPhones, up from 6% four years ago, according to Counterpoint Research.
  • The exemption also covers income from storing and supplying components to contract manufacturers.

From Five Years to Fifteen

India has proposed a dramatic extension of tax breaks for foreign electronics companies that supply equipment to local contract manufacturers, according to a draft amendment seen by Reuters. The new proposal would exempt foreign firms from tax on machinery ownership through March 31, 2041 — tripling the five-year window introduced in the February 2026 budget.

The original exemption, announced during Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman’s Union Budget 2026-27, addressed a long-standing concern for Apple. Under Indian law, if Apple paid for manufacturing machinery used by its contractors Foxconn and Tata, the arrangement could be classified as a “business connection” — potentially exposing Apple’s global iPhone profits to Indian taxation.

The amendment covers manufacturers of mobile phones, tablets, laptops, hearing devices, and wearable electronics — essentially the full spectrum of consumer electronics India wants produced domestically.

Apple’s India Manufacturing Push

The extended tax break comes as Apple rapidly scales its Indian manufacturing footprint. India is now set to produce 26% of the world’s iPhones in 2026, a fourfold increase from 6% in 2022, according to Counterpoint Research. Apple’s Indian market share has also doubled to 8% since 2022, while China’s share of global iPhone production has declined from 95% to 75%.

Without the tax exemption, Apple’s contract manufacturers Foxconn and Tata had been forced to bear the multi-billion-dollar cost of purchasing manufacturing equipment themselves. The new rules allow Apple to directly fund this machinery without triggering tax liabilities, reducing the financial burden on its Indian partners and accelerating production scale-up.

Broader Implications for Electronics Manufacturing

The amendment goes beyond smartphones. The draft bill extends the tax exemption to manufacturers of tablets, laptops, hearing devices, and wearable electronic devices. India has also proposed exempting foreign companies from tax on income earned from storing and providing parts to contract manufacturers.

The move aligns with Prime Minister Modi’s broader manufacturing agenda, which aims to make India a global electronics production hub. India’s electronics exports have grown from $10 billion in 2020 to over $30 billion in 2025, with smartphone exports — dominated by Apple — accounting for the bulk of the increase.

Parliamentary Approval Needed

The proposed amendment must be passed by both houses of parliament. Given that the ruling coalition holds a majority, passage is widely expected. The extension from 2031 to 2041 provides the long-term policy certainty that global manufacturers have sought, reducing the risk that tax rules change mid-investment cycle.
